series: Climate Fiscal Policy Brief No. 2.1 · October 2026
title: Taxing Rent, Not Effort

slides.title: Taxing Rent, Not Effort
slides.subtitle: Land and corporate taxation consistent with free movement of capital and people
slides.message: Free movement caps the rate on income that can move, not on rent that cannot. Tax land above a household allowance, and tax the rent of large firms where it cannot leave: at origin where it is tied to the place, at destination where it follows the customer.
slides.author: Stephen J. Stretton · writing in a personal capacity

slides.title: Rent can be taxed at high rates if the tax reaches it where it cannot leave

points.lead: Rent is income above what keeps an asset or a firm in use.
points.text: Taxing it changes nothing anyone does, so the rate can be high.

points.lead: Some rent is tied to a place:
points.text: land, natural resources, a large local market. Tax it at source.

points.lead: Some rent can be booked anywhere:
points.text: patents, brands, platforms. Tax it where the customer is.
Norway taxes petroleum profit at a marginal 78 percent, on a base that exempts the normal return.

slides.source: Mirrlees et al. (2011), ch. 18; Norwegian petroleum tax system (2025).

slides.title: Tax land above a household allowance, so large holdings pay and ordinary homes do not

points.lead: About 2.5 percent a year on site value
points.text: above an allowance close to the site value of an ordinary home. Business land taxed in full.
and its supply is fixed: the tax lowers land prices once and changes no use of land.
Pennsylvania cities that taxed land more than buildings saw more building and more housing units.
regular revaluation, a phased rate, and deferral for owners rich in land but poor in cash.

slides.source: Mirrlees et al. (2011), ch. 16; Oates and Schwab (1997); Banzhaf and Lavery (2010); OECD (2022).

slides.title: Presume that large firms earn rent, and tax only the profit above a normal return

points.lead: A firm that is large and stays large earns rent,
points.text: unless its industry can support only a few firms (civil aircraft, leading-edge chips).

points.lead: US markups rose from 21% to 61% above cost since 1980;
points.text: the measurement is disputed, and efficient firms' surplus is rent too.
deduct a normal return on equity, tax the rest at 50 percent for groups above €750 million.

points.lead: The marginal investment pays nothing at any rate,
points.text: so investment and innovation are not discouraged.

slides.source: De Loecker, Eeckhout and Unger (2020); Basu (2019); Boadway and Bruce (1984); Bond and Devereux (2003).

slides.title: A high rate at origin alone drives profit abroad, so two layers follow the customer

points.lead: Reported profit rises 1.5% for each point a country's rate is below others'.
points.text: Doubling the rate on rent could cut the declared base by over a third.
22 percent of local sales less local costs; royalties to related firms abroad not deductible.
4 percent of local sales, less credits of 8 percent of local assets and 25 percent of local payroll.
the destination layers stop at half the group's global rent margin times its local sales.

slides.source: Beer, de Mooij and Liu (2020); Devereux et al. (2021); OECD (2021).
